acceptanceCriteria: Policy accepts ticketBudget.overrides[] with exactly one selector (ticket, label or kind) and sessionsPerDay and/or tokensPerDay; malformed or ambiguous entries refuse with a stable code.
Precedence is defined and tested: ticket over label over kind over the default; ties among labels resolve deterministically.
The same rolling-window and exhaustion rules apply per effective limit.
dispatch status and the budget report show each ticket's effective limit, the selector that set it, and the hold reason.
Without overrides behaviour and output are unchanged.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1066 (2026-10-17), follow-up to #652/V1-0937. ticketBudget (CAL-V0-155) is one uniform {sessionsPerDay, tokensPerDay} for every ticket; observed queues need a productive ticket at ~56 sessions/day while stuck tickets need 6-8. Operators keep an external per-ticket cap file and wrapper, which duplicates budget logic and is invisible to dispatch status. Ask: ticketBudget.overrides[] keyed by ticket id and/or label or kind, same rolling-window and exhaustion rules; dispatch status shows the effective limit and why a ticket is held. New requirements go to the dispatch domain spec (ATR-V0 or its successor), not CAL-V0.
title: dispatch ticketBudget: per-ticket and per-label overrides with effective limit and hold reason in dispatch status (issue #1066)
